Advocate For The Appellant Praying That This Hon Ble
Court May Be Pleased To Allow The Appeal And Modify
The Impugned Judgment And Award Dated 24.07.2015
Passed By The Court Of The Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal No.Vii, Vijaypur, In Mvc No.287/2013 And
Enhance The Compensation As Pryed For.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDRERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the MACT-VII,
Vijaypur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.287/2013 dated 24.07.2015.
2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
On 21.11.2012 at about 7-00 a.m. when she was traveling in a Mahendra Maximo Jeep bearing No.MH-13/TC- 175 from Tamlawadi towards Solapur and inspite of telling the driver of the jeep to go in a safe and study manner but he did not care and drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed one Truck bearing No.RJ- 02/GA-1551 also came from opposite side resulting in the accident and the petitioner suffering grievous injuries.

Soon thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Yashodhara Hospital as an indoor patient from the date of accident till 30.11.2010 for about 10 days, that she was operated and steel rod was inserted of right radius and plaster put on right hand and that she has incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,00,000/- and that further medical expenses amounting to Rs.25,000/-.
petitioner submits that she cannot carry on her tailoring business as earlier she was doing.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she has been permanently disabled and lost source of income.
Thereby causing dent to her financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, she preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 3 remained absent and placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

2 6.

sentences.text: Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.1,77,920/-.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his argued that the tribunal has committed an error in exonerated the liability on the Bajaj Insurance company-respondent No.2, even if it is presumed that there is violation of policy terms and conditions then "principle of pay and recover" is applicable to the case on hand.
To substantiate his argument, he relied on the decision of Pappu and others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and others (2018) 3 SCC 208.

entities.text: Pappu and others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and others (2018) 3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further he has submitted that the tribunal has not properly determined the compensation and sought for just and proper compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the owner/insurer had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.

Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned,
injuries show that claimant had suffered permanent disability.

12. With regard to liability is concerned, that the tribunal has observed as under:
"Respondent No.2 Insurance company has contended that they are not at all liable to indemnify the petitioner since she is a paid passenger and insurance policy was for a private car package policy schedule and insurance policy has also been produced by the Insurance Company Bajaj Allianz respondent No.2.
Wherein, the policy has been marked as Ex.R3, It discloses that it is a private car package policy.
The premium paid is Rs.9350/-, seating capacity 8 passengers."

13. It is seen that, on the basis of the complaint filed by one Pharuk Khan Naharuke, the Solapur police have registered a case in Cr.No.196/2012 against the unknown driver of Mini Mahendra Magic Van No.Nil, and submitted FIR to the court.
Thereafter, the police have visited the spot and conducted spot mahazar, prepared rough sketch on the spot, recorded the statement of witnesses and submitted charge sheet against the accused.

Afzal Khan Pathan S/o Shabbirkhan Pathan the driver of the mini Mahendra vehicle without number for the commission of offence punishable under Section 279, 337,338 and 427 of IPC R/w section 183, 184 of MV Act.
14 . Further it is seen that the Investigating officer has not filed any charge sheet against the accused for violation of permit conditions or other conditions.

That the tribunal has observed that in the cross examination of PW1, has stated that four passengers boarded to the vehicle and Rs.20 fare has Uma W/O Mahesh Shelawane vs Sambhaji S/O Shivaji Sulukhe And Ors on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55283359/
3 been paid from Tamalvadi to Sollapur.

entities.text: Uma W/O Mahesh Shelawane vs Sambhaji S/O Shivaji Sulukhe And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Only on the basis of this stray admission, the tribunal has held that the owner of the vehicle violated permit conditions.
Mere stray admission of PW1 is not sufficient to come to the conclusion that they are fare paid passengers.
Hence, in this regard the tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record.
Apart from this, Ex.R3-the private car package policy reveals that the insurance company has received an amount of Rs.400/- P.A cover for 8 passengers.
Therefore, the insurance company cannot escape from its liability.
The tribunal has committed an error in this regard.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner, respondent No.2 being the Insurance company are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
And the doctor has not at all mentioned the injury regarding nature of the wound and considering the nature of above injury No.1 will be simple injury and injuries No.2 to 4 are grievous in nature.

15. Ex.P10 is the disability certificate on perusing the same, the disability certificate issued by PW2 Dr. Ashok Nayak, he has given the percentage of the disability 20% to 25% to that part of the limb portion.

PW2/doctor has been cross- examined and in the cross-examination, he has clearly admitted that he has not at all treated doctor and he denies in the cross-examination that the percentage of the disability given by him is on the higher side.

However, considering the nature and extent of injuries suffered by the petitioner and also considering the fact that the petitioner was doing household work and tailoring business, it would be appropriate and just that the percentage of the disability be taken as 8%.
16.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2012, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.6,500/- p.m.
The claimant is aged about 28 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,06,080/-
(Rs.6,500/- x 12 x 17 x 8%) on account of 'loss of future income'.

4 17.

Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re- determined and re-calculated as under:-
 Sl.

Heads  No Tribunal Court  01 Towards pain and Rs.30,000/- Rs.35,000/-
 suffering

02 Medical expenses, Rs.30,000/- Rs.30,000/-
 03 Loss of future income Rs.97,920/- Rs.1,06,080/-

04 Loss of amenities Rs.20,000/- Rs.30,000/-
 05

Towards attendant ---- Rs.10,000/-
 and diet charges  06 Loss of income ---- Rs.30,000/-
 during laid up period  Total Rs.1,77,920/- Rs.2,41,080/-
18. In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER  (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.287/2013 dated 24.07.2015 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.1,77,920/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,41,080/-.

(c) The insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
- 10 - (d) The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
